summary: Feed s091_single is degraded: SIEM port (1 Gbps) is severely overloaded by microbursts up to 4.23 Gbps (423% capacity). All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, one-way, drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding aggregated/bursty traffic directly to a single 1 Gbps SIEM ingest port without shaping or load distribution. 1 ms microbursts peak at 4.23 Gbps, exceeding the physical port capacity by 4.2x across 3 intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC buffer overruns and drops excess packets during bursts. Results in missing flow/event records, incomplete correlation, and blind spots for detection despite SIEM not requiring full payload or bidirectional traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute microbursts across a SIEM ingest pool (or add packet broker egress ports) so aggregate capacity exceeds 4.23 Gbps peak. SIEM tolerates flow-level distribution (needs_both_directions=false) and 5-tuple hashing preserves flow coherence. Alternative/complementary: enable slicing/filtering since SIEM needs_full_payload=false to further reduce bps.
